alt: Poster: Equity mutual fund gains tax rules - 20% short-term, 12.5% long-term, Rs 1,25,000 long-term gains exemption per financial year
text:
Equity mutual fund gains are taxed on two clocks, not one.

For units of equity-oriented funds, the holding period decides the bucket: 12 months or less is short-term, taxed at 20%. More than 12 months is long-term, taxed at 12.5% without indexation. These rates apply to transfers on or after 23 July 2024 and are published on the Income Tax Department's website.

On long-term gains, the first Rs 1,25,000 in a financial year is not taxed; tax is calculated only on the excess. The concessional rates apply where Securities Transaction Tax (STT) was paid on the transfer.

Our reading: the 12-month mark and the Rs 1,25,000 threshold are the two numbers worth checking before any redemption date is fixed. This is an interpretation, not advice.

For practitioners: how do you present realised-gain statements to families so the short-term and long-term split is easy to follow?
